originality.rationale: Qualitative nonreal sketched SPD eigenvalues already appear in the 2024 and 2026 primary sources; claim excludes them. The new assessed content is the exact optimal spectral-width/angle envelope, equality at every nonzero angle, and zero-angle rigidity. Direct primary full text and queried mathematical records produced no covering statement. General Kahan-type bounds and uninspected historical oblique-projection literature leave genuine priority risk. Closest accessible historical finding 15c0a9d2-0140-449c-9962-650e34d56964 obtains the same profile only by optimizing its constrained three-state E-optimal Krylov family. Its existential lower bound does not imply the new universal upper bound over all SPD matrices and all two-planes at fixed gamma. Historical finding ff54842f-13da-4a36-870a-5eeacc4276e5 assumes sketch embedding on span{Q,AQ}; sharpness here uses a full 3D span annihilated on one coordinate, violating that embedding hypothesis, and the prior residual-gap bound does not imply the new envelope.
residual_risks: An older theorem on oblique compressions or numerical ranges may specialize to the same sharp constant despite different vocabulary.
Hrobat–Nakatsukasa appendices, Kahan primary proof, Carden–Embree full paper and Haas–Nakatsukasa full paper were not exhaustively inspected; no whole-document noncoverage is asserted for them.
Search and database nonhits are not proof of historical uniqueness.

The sharp constant appeared previously as a restricted-family supremum; novelty rests on proving the global inequality. A more general known oblique-compression bound could subsume that proof even if not found.
